Guides › No sign-up

Free AI video generators, no sign-up

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

VidFare tracks nine models. On the seller pages that included plan text Nov 20, 2026, 7:05 PM ET (4:05 PM PT), none of them publishes a way to generate a video with no account. Wan 3.0, Wan 3.0 Prime, and Kling 3.0 are separate models, and their plan pages did not include plan text on this check. Outside the catalog, Hugging Face documents 2 minutes of GPU time a day with no account, from Hugging Face ZeroGPU documentation. DeepAI sells pay-per-call video with no account. Vheer’s home page says no signup; its pricing page lists a monthly credit cap, so the video terms are not clear. We did not run a generation. For free tiers that do use an account, see free AI video generators: what you get.

Last checked 2026-11-25. Official pages were read Nov 20, 2026, 7:05 PM ET (4:05 PM PT). Catalog rows use the date on each row. Affiliate links never change this price order. Every dollar-per-second figure below names its seller and states its usage assumption, tier, resolution, and audio.

Key takeaways

  • Nine catalog models. Wan 3.0 Prime, Wan 3.0, Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1, Gemini Omni Flash, MiniMax Hailuo, Runway Gen-4, and Grok Imagine. Krea, Pika, Luma, Meta AI, Vheer, DeepAI, and Hugging Face are outside the catalog and are labelled that way.
  • No catalog model published a no-account path on a seller page that loaded. Wan, Wan 3.0 Prime, and Kling could not be re-read.
  • Documented no-account route. Hugging Face Spaces: 2 minutes of GPU time a day, low queue priority. Clips per day: not published.
  • Paid, no account. DeepAI, $0.20/s on DeepAI for HD at 720p. Audio is not stated.
  • Claimed, and contradicted on the same site. Vheer’s home page says unlimited and no signup. Its pricing page lists 50 credits a month. Not tested. SeeDance V1 on that site is not Seedance 2.5.
  • Least account with a published allowance. Krea: free account, no card, 100 units a day, no watermark, personal use. Not in the catalog.

Is there a paid option with no account?

Yes. DeepAI’s video page says people with no account can buy video pay-per-call at $0.20 per second for HD at 720p and $0.30 per second for Hollywood mode at 2K. Audio is not stated. DeepAI Pro is $9.99 a month and includes the first 25 seconds of standard video and the first 8 seconds of 2K Hollywood mode. This page does not turn that bundle into a per-second rate. The lowest rate in the VidFare catalog is $0.0113 per second for Wan 3.0 on Higgsfield (Ultra (annual), 480p, audio not stated, from credit plan, catalog row r096, checked 2026-11-26). The lowest published rates are $0.02 per second for grok_imagine_1_5_lite (480p) on Runway API at 480p, audio not stated (catalog row r055, checked 2026-11-26), $0.02 per second for grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite on xAI API at 480p, audio not stated (catalog row r209, checked 2026-11-26). Those catalog routes need an account. The table is in price order.

    Which free AI video generators work with no sign-up?

    Hugging Face documents one no-account route: an unauthenticated visitor gets 2 minutes of GPU time a day on hosted demo Spaces, at low queue priority. DeepAI documents a no-account route that is paid, at $0.20 per second for HD at 720p and $0.30 per second for Hollywood mode at 2K. Vheer’s home page says generations are unlimited with no signup, while its pricing page lists a Free plan of 50 credits a month, so what applies to video without an account is not clear. None of the nine catalog models has a no-account path on a seller page that loaded on Nov 20, 2026. Wan’s and Kling’s plan pages did not include plan text, so those three model rows (Wan 3.0, Wan 3.0 Prime, and Kling 3.0) are not re-confirmed. We did not run a generation.

    Do the catalog models need an account to generate video?

    Where the seller page loaded, yes. Google Flow, which serves Veo 3.1 and the Omni Flash line, requires age 18 or older and a supported region, and its 50 daily credits are shared across your account. The catalog model is Gemini Omni Flash 1.1; the Flow page read Nov 20, 2026 prices Omni Flash 1.2 and says Omni Flash 1.1 retires on December 5, 2026. Dreamina, the consumer seller for Seedance 2.5, ties free credits to the credits in your account and shows Sign in. Hailuo’s terms give free users video generation upon logging in. Runway’s pricing page describes a Free plan with a one-time deposit of 125 credits. Higgsfield says every new account starts on the free plan, which has no monthly credits. Grok Imagine’s consumer page did not state a no-account video path, and x.ai/grok returned 403. Wan 3.0, Wan 3.0 Prime, and Kling 3.0 are separate catalog models whose plan pages did not include plan text on Nov 20, 2026. Higgsfield sells several of these models. Higgsfield help: what the free plan includes, read Nov 20, 2026, 7:05 PM ET (4:05 PM PT), says every new account starts on the free plan, the plan has no monthly credits, models on it still deduct credits, and a watermark can appear. That is an account. Which of the nine models are in the free set is not stated. Higgsfield pricing explained.

    What is the least sign-up with a published allowance?

    If an account with no card is acceptable, Krea is the seller that states it: a free account, no credit card, 100 units a day, and no watermark. Krea is not in the VidFare catalog, and free-plan videos are for personal use. Google Flow publishes 50 credits a day, about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips at 720p if every credit goes to Lite, for an account that meets the age and region rules. Hugging Face publishes a no-account allowance in minutes of GPU time, not in clips. A best-for line is given only where the provider’s page supports it.

    • Hugging Face Spaces. Best for: the no-account allowance a provider states as a number, 2 minutes of GPU time a day. Not for: a known clip count, which is not published, or a fast queue, because unauthenticated use is low priority. Hugging Face ZeroGPU documentation.
    • Krea, with a free account. Best for: no credit card, 100 units a day, and no watermark, all stated by Krea. Not for: commercial work, because Krea says free-plan videos are for personal use, or for Seedance 2.5 and Veo 3.1, which need Pro or higher. Not in the VidFare catalog. Krea’s AI video generator page · Krea’s pricing page.
    • Google Flow, with an account. Best for: a daily amount you can count, 50 credits, about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips at 720p if every credit goes to Lite. Not for: skipping the age and region rules, or generating during the peak hours the credit help page names, without a paid plan. Related: Google Flow credits calculator · Veo 3.1 · Gemini Omni Flash.

    No line given. Vheer, Perchance, Meta AI, the Grok consumer site, Wan, and Kling do not have a best-for line: the pages we could read do not support one, or they did not load.

    What to do next

    • Check the vendor page. No-account access can change without notice. Open Hugging Face ZeroGPU documentation or DeepAI’s video page and confirm the terms before you rely on them.
    • Try the calculator. If you end up paying, put your clip length into the credit calculator.
    • Open the model page. Every current catalog rate, with its source and date: Veo 3.1 · Gemini Omni Flash · Wan 3.0 · Wan 3.0 Prime · Grok Imagine.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page.
